decisions.reason: The client explicitly preserves the Hero V's established slope and structure; only the separately represented shared terminal treatment changes.
The source preserves the second V's established geometry while changing the separately represented shared terminal treatment, so its glyph-geometry state remains valid.
The terminal refinement applies only to the Hero V, second V, and É accent and does not change the E or L letterform requirements.
The source changes terminal character while preserving the second V's structure; it does not alter any relative-height or prominence rule.
The same message's kerning decision is already represented by a complete MODIFY selecting Option 2 Balanced Flow and removing the obsolete exploratory spacing direction.
Refining the shared terminal does not change the requirement that the Hero V and É accent peaks align exactly.
The É accent must continue to use the literal Hero V terminal; the source changes that shared terminal's character but not the accent's derivation rule.
The source sequences terminal refinement before further material work but does not change the selected Satin Reflection finish, gold distribution, or material constraints.
The shared terminal refinement does not alter the E/L cap-height relationship to the second V's left arm.
The source does not change the common-baseline alignment of the wordmark.
The source supplies design direction for the terminal but does not change the obligation to include rationale with review rounds.
